subject: Re: Commercial structure for Novacorp pilot — credits vs margin-preserve
messages:

Date: Tue, 18 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Commercial structure for pilot — need margin-preserve option

Stephanie / Rishi —

Thanks again for the pilot proposal you sent last week. Procurement reviewed and flagged two sticking points: the credit-heavy onboarding structure reduces our vendor margin and complicates our internal cost allocations. They asked whether Redwood can present an alternative that keeps Novacorp's vendor margins intact (no large upfront credits) while still allowing Redwood to protect unit economics — essentially a "margin-preserve" option.

Can you send a short-side by side (bulleted) of: 1) credit-led pilot (what you sent) vs 2) margin-preserve (smaller credits + slightly higher per-token rate or longer commit) — and a recommended path? Procurement would like pricing anchors by EOD Friday so they can include it in their supplier evaluation.

Appreciate a crisp comparison. Happy to hop on a 20-min call if useful.

Best,
Olivia Park
Director, Cloud Procurement
Novacorp

---
(Attachment: novacorp-cost-model.xlsx)

From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
To: Olivia Park <olivia.park@novacorp.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 18 May 2027 11:06:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Commercial structure for pilot — need margin-preserve option

Olivia —

Thanks for the clear ask. Attached is a short side-by-side and an initial term sheet (redwood-pilot-term-sheet-v1.pdf) plus the cost model populated with your baseline usage. High level summary below:

Option A — Credit-led pilot (original)
- Upfront onboarding credit: $120k applied to first 3 months
- Lower per-token rate during pilot (15% discount)
- Redwood absorbs initial integration support hours (up to 40 hours)
- Best if Novacorp wants minimal churn risk during first 90 days

Option B — Margin-preserve pilot (new)
- Reduced onboarding credit: $40k one-time
- Slightly higher per-token rate during pilot (5% discount vs list)
- 6-month minimum commitment (to offset unit economics)
- Performance SLA uplift optional (revenue-share style uplift available if SLA met)

Our recommendation: If procurement needs to maintain vendor margin accounting, Option B with a 6-month commit and a small credit is the cleanest path. It keeps your bookkeeping simple and gives Redwood runway to hit steady-state throughput without excessive upfront concession.

I've cc'd Rishi/Marcus to confirm this is deliverable from the pricing/finance side — Marcus, can we model the expected ARR impact if they choose Option B vs A (assume 6-month pilot, projected volume in the attached sheet)?

Quick note on timelines: if Novacorp wants a final term sheet and DocuSign by Friday, we can get V1 -> V2 updated once we agree the concession structure.

Thanks,

Stephanie Nguyen
Head of Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
(Attachment: redwood-pilot-term-sheet-v1.pdf; novacorp-cost-model.xlsx)

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 19 May 2027 09:15:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Commercial structure for pilot — need margin-preserve option

Team —

Reviewed Stephanie's draft. Quick internal take (numbers back-of-envelope):
- Option B (reduced credit + 6m commit) keeps blended unit economics within acceptable band if we: (a) keep the per-token uplift capped at +4% vs list during pilot and (b) limit included support to 30 hours instead of 40.
- If Novacorp asks for SLA uplift (99.9% to 99.95%), we should price SLA credit as a separate add-on rather than bake into the base rate. That's easier to justify to finance and preserves headline margin.
- Suggested counter: offer Option B with $40k credit, 6m minimum, per-token at +2% vs our standard pilot discount, and SLA add-on priced at $5k/month. If Novacorp pushes hard, we can convert $10k of the credit into training/enablement credits to avoid straight cash concessions.

Marcus — can you run the ARR delta and margin impact with those tweaks and post results here by EOD? I'll prep suggested wording for the term sheet so it's clear what is concession vs commercial engineering.

Rishi
VP, Commercial Operations

On Wed, May 19, 2027 at 09:36 Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com> wrote:
> Thanks Rishi — that framing works. Marcus, let us know the ARR delta and we can finalize V2.

From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>

Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, Novacorp Procurement <procurement@novacorp.com>
Date: Thu, 20 May 2027 14:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Updated: Pilot commercial — margin-preserve option and final term sheet (v2)

Olivia / Ethan / procurement team —

Appreciate the quick turnaround. Per our internal alignment (cc'd Rishi/Marcus/Lauren), attached is a revised term sheet (redwood-pilot-term-sheet-v2.pdf) and an updated cost model (novacorp-cost-model-v2.xlsx) that reflect the margin-preserve path. Highlights: 

- Reduced onboarding credit: $40,000 (applied to month 1)
- Pilot length: 6 months minimum commitment
- Pilot pricing: list rate less 10% (net of previous draft) — this is a modest premium vs credit-led option but preserves your margins; see line items in the cost model
- Support: up to 30 professional hours included; further hours available at contracted rates
- SLA uplift: optional add-on at $5k/month (99.95% target; credit structure detailed in section 4)
- Cancellation: 60-day notice after pilot period; early termination fee equal to remaining pilot months at 50% of contracted MRR (keeps both parties aligned)

Link to DocuSign for the term sheet (if you want to fast-track): https://app.docusign.com/documents/XYZ-987654

If that looks generally good, can we get procurement's confirmation on the invoicing cadence (monthly in arrears vs net-30 invoice on pilot draw)? That is the remaining open invoicing point Rishi flagged as material for finance.

Next steps suggested:
1) Procurement confirms invoicing cadence by EOD tomorrow
2) Optional 20-min alignment call if you want to walk the tradeoffs live
3) We send final DocuSign and aim for signature next week

Thanks — happy to jump on a call to walk through any line items.

Best,
Stephanie Nguyen
Head of Strategic Accounts, Redwood Inference
(Attachments: redwood-pilot-term-sheet-v2.pdf; novacorp-cost-model-v2.xlsx)

Subject: Re: Updated: Pilot commercial — margin-preserve option and final term sheet (v2)

Stephanie —

Thanks for the quick update and the clear comparison. Procurement reviewed V2 and is generally supportive of Option B (margin-preserve) with the $40k credit + 6-month commit. Two small asks before we sign: 

1) Invoicing cadence: Novacorp prefers monthly in arrears. Will Redwood accept monthly invoices vs net-30 invoice on pilot draw? (procurement: it simplifies our accounting).
2) Can you convert $5k of the onboarding credit into a one-time professional services line (for our onboarding PM) rather than an unrestricted credit? That helps us justify the spend internally.

If you accept those, we're comfortable moving to DocuSign and aiming for signature early next week. We can book a 20-min call Monday morning to finalize language if needed.

Appreciate the partnership here.

Regards,
Olivia Park
Director, Cloud Procurement
Novacorp
